tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

<skill_instructions>
# SAGE-Kit

SAGE-Kit is a single-user, local, single-repository task tracker. Task state lives in
files under `.sage-kit/` and is written by the `sage-kit` CLI. It is not a service:
there is no daemon, no HTTP API, no database connection, and no network call.

## Project root

The CLI resolves the **project root** as the nearest ancestor directory that contains
`.git`. When no such directory exists (for example a scratch directory that is not a
git repository), it uses the current working directory. Configuration is then read from
`<project-root>/.sage-kit/config.json`; the CLI does not search parent directories for
the config file.

## When to use

Use this skill when **all** of these are true:

- `.sage-kit/config.json` exists at the resolved project root (run
  `sage-kit doctor --json` if the root or config state is unclear).
- The work is a coding task in this repository.
- The user asks to create, inspect, update, brief, or finish a tracked task.

Do not use SAGE-Kit for one-off shell commands, writing prose, or a different project.

## Commands

Run commands from anywhere inside the repository; they act on the resolved project root.
If the package is not installed locally/globally, use the tarball or `node dist/cli.js`
from a checkout — the package is not published on the npm registry yet.

```text
sage-kit task create --title "<title>" --description "<why>" --acceptance "<criterion>"
sage-kit task list
sage-kit task show <id> --json
sage-kit task status <id> running
sage-kit task status <id> review
sage-kit task status <id> done --evidence "file:line or command output"
sage-kit brief --task <id> --max-bytes 2048
sage-kit doctor --json
```

Task statuses: `imported`, `ready`, `running`, `review`, `done`, `blocked`, `failed`,
`cancelled`, `interrupted`. The CLI enforces transitions: a new task starts `ready`,
and `done` is only reachable from `review` (running/ready → done is rejected). A task
can move `running → review → done`; record evidence on the `review → done` step.

## Rules

1. Create or select one task before substantial edits. Keep one active task.
2. Read the task brief before editing; it is the bounded context, not a replacement for
   the repository's own instructions. `sage-kit brief` prints the current brief;
   `SESSION_BRIEF.md` at the project root is an init-time snapshot and may be stale.
3. `done` requires at least one evidence item. If the acceptance criteria are not met,
   leave the task `running`, `review`, or `blocked` — do not claim completion.
4. Never fabricate evidence. Evidence is a pointer (file, test, exact command output),
   not a claim of success.
5. Task files under `.sage-kit/state/tasks/<id>.json` are the source of truth; events are
   appended to `.sage-kit/state/events/events.jsonl`; run records live under
   `.sage-kit/state/runs/`. Do not hand-edit a task file while the CLI may be writing.
6. This skill is stateless. It does not start a server, hold a database connection, or
   make network calls. The CLI reads/writes local files only.
7. Hooks are optional and advisory, and `init` does **not** install host hooks. When the
   host or user calls `sage-kit hook`, honor a `warn` message and never ignore a `block`
   action. Without hook wiring, generate the brief manually with `sage-kit brief`; a
   missing hook is a limitation to report, never evidence of success.

## Host notes

- **DSH:** repository instructions are `AGENTS.md`; the project skill is installed at
  `.dsh/skills/sage-kit/`. A real DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 headless session with a **mock model**
  discovered and loaded that folder (real model/GUI acceptance is `NOT_EXECUTED`). That
  DSH version exposes no installable native third-party hook config, so `session.start`
  is not injected automatically.
- **Codex:** repository instructions are `AGENTS.md`; the file adapter installs the skill
  into the project's `.agents/skills/sage-kit/`. Real Codex session discovery is
  `NOT_VERIFIED`.
- **Claude Code:** repository instructions are `CLAUDE.md`; the file adapter installs the
  skill into `.claude/skills/sage-kit/`. Real Claude session discovery is `NOT_VERIFIED`.

If the host does not discover project skills, still use the CLI directly; the skill is
convenience, not a runtime requirement.
</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>
